title: Local evaluation comparisons with a K-injective second representative
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] on $X$ and every open, let $K,N\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, and let $U$ be open. Write $R$ for restriction and $H$ for derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $P,F$ be complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, with $F$ K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and $P$ strictly perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], and suppose given isomorphisms $RK\cong QP$ and $RN\cong QF$. Suppose given a chain map $f:T=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\mathcal O_U[0]))\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ satisfying the ordinary evaluation formula [lem-pc-strictly-perfect-ordinary-evaluation]. Put $D=H(K,\mathcal O_X[0])$, and let $g:N\otimes^L D\to H(K,N)$ be the canonical adjunct of the associator followed by $1_N\otimes\mathrm{ev}$ and the right unitor, for [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] and [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. There exist compatible isomorphisms $a:R(N\otimes^L D)\cong QT$ and $b:RH(K,N)\cong Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ such that $R(g);b=a;Q(f)$. The complexes, representative isomorphisms and ordinary chain map are inputs, not objects asserted to exist.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_strictlyPerfect_kInjective_evaluation_comparisons (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (K N : schemeDerivedCategory X) (U : X.Opens)
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    [F.IsKInjective]
    (_hstrict : Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect X U P)
    (_eK : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
    (_eN : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj N ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj F)
    (f : localEvaluationTensor X U P F ⟶ homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P F)
    (_hf : IsLocalOrdinaryEvaluation X U P F f) :
    let R := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
      X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let D := H.obj (op K, 𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X))
    let g := ((schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X) (N ⊗ D) K N).symm
      ((α_ N D K).hom ≫ N ◁
        ((schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X) D K (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X)) (𝟙 D)) ≫
          (ρ_ N).hom)
    ∃ a : R.obj (N ⊗ D) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (localEvaluationTensor X U P F),
      ∃ b : R.obj (H.obj (op K, N)) ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj (homComplex (R := X.sheaf.over U) P F),
        R.map g ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map f

proof.text: Restrict derived internal Hom to U and transport through eK and eN. The second model F is already K-injective, so derivedInternalHom_obj_iso computes the target as Q Hom(P,F) directly, supplying b without any quasi-isomorphism calculation for F.

Apply the same computation to O_U[0]. The dual degree-q term is the dual of P^(-q); dualizing its finite-free retraction shows that it is finite projective and flat. The bounded dual is K-flat. Hence tensoring it with arbitrary F computes the derived tensor. Exact restriction and the given representative of N supply a, with symmetry used when the K-flat factor is second.

Apply the canonical tensor-Hom representative equation with the already K-injective target F. Uncurrying each tensor summand gives evaluation of the dual on P and the unit action on F, exactly hf. The coproduct inclusions and Hom projections detect equality. Localize and transport through the same restriction and representative comparisons to obtain the displayed square; no resolution of F or Hom(P,-) quasi-isomorphism preservation is required here.
